findings.problem: BudgetWorkflow uses pub String for status, allowing any arbitrary string value including illegal combinations like status="pending" with is_sent=true.
findings.failure_mode: Domain invariants cannot be enforced by the compiler; callers can construct a BudgetWorkflow that represents an impossible state (e.g., marked sent but with a non-sent status string).
findings.fix: Replace pub status: String with a domain enum such as pub status: BudgetStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent } and remove is_sent boolean field entirely.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are primitive lifecycle flags that allow inconsistent state (e.g., is_sent=true with status!="sent").
findings.failure_mode: Two separate pieces of truth about workflow lifecycle; one can be set without the other, producing inconsistent state that runtime checks would catch but the type system cannot.
findings.fix: Replace both bools with a single BudgetStatus enum that encodes all valid lifecycle transitions as distinct variants.

findings.problem: mark_sent takes ownership and mutates the struct in-place rather than returning a new state via an immutable transition. This is a mutable-shell pattern leaking into what should be a pure core.
findings.failure_mode: No explicit lifecycle ordering can be verified; callers can call mark_sent on any BudgetWorkflow regardless of prior state (e.g., double-sending), and the function performs string allocation ("sent".to_string()) instead of a zero-copy enum transition.
findings.fix: Replace mark_sent with a pure transition function such as fn into_sent(self) -> Result<BudgetWorkflow, TransitionError> that validates preconditions and returns a new typed state, or encode the transition as a method on an enum-based typestate.

findings.problem: pub id: String accepts any string; there is no domain-type newtype for id, no validation, and no fallible constructor.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid or empty IDs can be constructed directly; no boundary parsing or validation layer exists.
findings.fix: Introduce a BudgetId newtype with a fallible constructor (e.g., fn try_from(s: &str) -> Result<BudgetId, ParseIdError>) and use it in BudgetWorkflow.

findings.problem: All fields of BudgetWorkflow are pub, allowing external code to mutate any field directly, bypassing any invariants the type is supposed to enforce.
findings.failure_mode: External code can do item.is_sent = false; item.status = ""; and produce a corrupted state without any constructor or transition function.
findings.fix: Make all fields private and provide only immutable accessors or transition methods. Use private fields with a public constructor that enforces invariants.

findings.problem: mark_sent allocates a new String via "sent".to_string() and also stores a String for id. No allocation avoidance strategy or arena/borrowed alternative is used.
findings.failure_mode: Hot-path allocation on every transition; no measurement or evidence that this allocation budget is acceptable.
findings.fix: Use a BudgetStatus enum (zero-cost representation) instead of String for status. For id, consider &str lifetime parameterization or a BudgetId newtype backed by an arena if shared ownership is needed.

findings.problem: mark_sent has no error return type; it cannot fail. If there are preconditions (e.g., must be validated before sent), there is no way to express them.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid transitions are silently accepted; the function is fallible in practice but declares infallibility in its signature.
findings.fix: Change signature to fn into_sent(self) -> Result<BudgetWorkflow, BudgetTransitionError> and define a domain error enum for invalid transitions.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists to measure transition latency or allocation cost

no allocation tracking or audit (Vec::with_capacity, String::to_string, etc.)
no command evidence: cargo fmt, cargo clippy, or cargo test were not run

residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The crate is fundamentally not Holzman-compliant: illegal states are representable via pub String/bool fields, no domain types exist, mark_sent mutates in place with no precondition checks, and there is zero evidence (no benchmarks, no tests, no clippy/fmt runs). The code shape needs a complete type-level redesign before any performance or verification work is meaningful.
